text:
CHI won 4-2 in a game STL controlled for most of the night. At even strength, STL generated 2.12 expected goals to CHI's 1.07, and the simulated replays give STL a 74 percent chance to win this game. The Blackhawks got there on a short-handed goal and an empty-net-style finish in the last two minutes, not on sustained pressure.

The scoring started with Mason McTavish's wrist shot late in the first, a 9 percent look that put STL up 1-0. CHI answered twice in the second, with Sam Rinzel scoring on the power play and Anton Frondell adding a snap shot two minutes later. STL then piled up chances in the third, outpacing CHI 2.06 to 0.28 in expected goals on that stretch of play (the data counts CHI's third-period total as 1.81, which includes the late goals). Dylan Holloway had STL's best look that didn't go in, an 18 percent chance that Spencer Knight stopped.

The game turned in the last 70 seconds. Cole Smith scored short-handed at 18:51, a 67 percent chance, to make it 3-1. Connor McMichael got one back on the power play 30 seconds later, but Frank Nazar's backhand at 19:56, an 87 percent chance, sealed it. Knight saved 1.18 goals more than the shots against him deserved, and he was named first star. Joel Hofer's 17 saves on 19 shots were close to what the chances called for.
